newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP sees copper demand strong.
newsitem.headline: BHP sees copper demand strong.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the world's second largest copper producer, said on Thursday that strong world demand for copper would allow the market to absorb new supplies.
"At a growth rtate of three to four percent per annum, it does not take long for that demand to absorb significnant projects," Jim Lewis, head of BHP's copper division, told reporters.
Lewis said that although substantial growth in world supply is scheduled to come on-stream in about two years, he doubted if every project would be completed by that time.
"We are quite firm in our expectations of copper prices going forward. We don't see a major collapse," Lewis said.
"We think that there is more strength in the market than what some of the other future soothsayers see," he added.

BHP reported a 32.2 percent fall in profits from its copper division to A$217 million in the six months to November 30, 1996. BHP Copper had a difficult 1996 year with a falling metal price after it purchased Magma Copper for US$2.4 billion.
Lewis told reporters earlier on Thursday that copper production costs at Magma were averaging around 80 U.S. cents a pound, owing in part to recent low ore grades at its Kalamazoo, Arizona mine.
This compares with about 68 cents a pound at the time of the Magma acquisition.
Costs at the BHP copper operations had fallen in the last three or four months, BHP chief executive officer John Prescott said last month.
Late last year, BHP said production costs in North America were running at about 70 cents U.S. a pound in the financial quarter ended November 30.
